title: Golf Course Architect 2 - The Back Nine
author: sacker
rules:
After designing your first nine holes, something's still missing. There’s an emptiness in your gut, a vacuum in your soul. And suddenly you hear it: an echo in the hills beyond. There’s more fairway to forge. More sand to sweep. More dimpled polymer to pummel. You’re here to finish what you started. Today, the second half is yours to take. Today, the back nine is yours to make. Today, much like a few days ago, you’re a golf course architect.

Solve this puzzle in SudokuPad.

Golf Course Design (Chaos Construction): Divide the grid into nine orthogonally connected regions of nine cells each. Each row, column, and region must contain the digits 1–9 exactly once.

Tee Boxes and Hole Numbers (Killer Cages): The back nine is to be played from holes 10-18, in order. Each hole (region) begins at a singular tee box cell. Each hole’s tee box cell is one of the cells within the hole’s corresponding cage, where the number in each cage indicates the hole number and the sum of the digits within the cage. The entire cage lies within its corresponding region.

Par: Each tee box cell is orthogonally adjacent to only one other cell in its region. The digit in this “second” cell for each region represents the hole’s par.

Flags: Each flag cell is the final cell in its region; it is orthogonally adjacent to the subsequent tee box cell. (And the 18th flag is orthogonally adjacent to the 10th tee box cell.) The flag cell is also orthogonally adjacent to only one other cell in its region.

Bunkers (Dutch Whispers): Adjacent digits along an orange bunker line differ by at least 4. Digits along the same bunker must be within the same region.

Unmown Grass (German Whisper): Adjacent digits along the green grass line differ by at least 5.

Pond (Filled Kropki Dot): The blue dot connects two digits with a ratio of 1:2 (one digit is double the other), and is located between a flag and the subsequent tee box cell.

Found Golf Ball (White Kropki Dot): The white dot connects two consecutive digits. (Solvers looking for an extra challenge don't need to use this golf ball.)

Playing Golf: After the back nine is constructed, you give it a whirl. As with the front nine, the digit in the flag cell represents your score for that hole. After the 9-hole round, you improve upon your front nine and score 2 under par on these 9 holes (in other words, the sum of the flag cells is 2 fewer than the sum of the par cells).
solutionCode: Your scorecard (the flag cells from holes 10-18, in order)
